newsitem.title: UK: British unemployment double official rate - report.
newsitem.headline: British unemployment double official rate - report.

text.p: British unemployment is more than double the official rate because large numbers of the jobless are hidden from the official figures, a new study said on Friday.
A research team at Sheffield Hallam University said that in January there were 3.9 million people out of work in the UK compared with the official monthly claimant count of 1.8 million.
The difference was accounted for by unemployed people ineligible for benefits, those on government schemes or long-term jobless regarded as retired early or permanently sick.
"The official unemployment figures are at odds with many people's first hand experience, especially in the areas of severe job losses," said Professor Stephen Fothergill, leader of the research team.

"What our figures show is that while the official figures may be correct within the narrow confines of what they set out to measure, ordinary people are correct in telling the government statisticians that unemployment is far more widespread."
The researchers said 1.2 million long-term unemployed were excluded from the official monthly figures because they claim incapacity benefit.
